newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves plan to sell 25 percent stake in Bezeq.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves plan to sell 25 percent stake in Bezeq.

text.p: Israel approved a plan to sell 25 percent of Bezeq, the country's main telecommunications carrier, which will reduce its holding to 51 percent by the end of the year, a government official said Thursday.

At the same time Bezeq's board announced it had named Ami Erel as its managing director. Erel, a 50-year-old engineer, was for the last seven years managing director of the Idan-Elitec group, which also provides telecommunications services and products.
Bezeq has seen its monopoly gradually whittled down over the years but retains monopolies in basic services and infrastructure.

Moshe Leon, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's chief economics adviser, said the plan to sell 25 percent of Bezeq called for selling part of the shares -- probably 10 percent -- through a public offering in the Israeli capital market.
The rest would be sold by means yet to be determined, he said.
The Israeli government holds 76 percent of Bezeq. The rest trades on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, although about half of those shares are controlled by Cable and Wireless PLC of Britain.
Israel has been in lengthy negotiations with Cable and Wireless over the company's future role in Bezeq, but officials said no agreement had yet been reached.
